title: Curtain Time and Laugh Time shows, then the Loew's and Poli circuits
summary: Agents Paul Small and Finklehoffe put on revue shows with Connie Boswell and Jack Haley in California, then the act worked Loew's and Poli in the East.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: That's where I actually go from Riverside, leaving Frank Sinatra and go back to -- let's see, where do we go from there. 1920, 1921 -- I've forgotten what year that was, 1921. I'm going to California now on the Pantages circuit. I left the Pantages circuit -- was that then -- I can take that later -- I can take Paul Small next and Finkelhoff, they were agents for a show called "Curtain Time," "Laugh Time" and "Show

Time." These are different shows that they put on that we were in with them where we had Connie Boswell, Jack Haley. We had George Jessel and this colored act called Miller Brothers and Lois, that's a dance act --

They danced on a pedestal, you know, same thing. However, those shows at the Curran Theater in San Francisco, they would have like the Biltmore Hotel in Los Angeles -- the Pantages Theater -- no it didn't get to the Pantages Theater at that.

We did that then we come back to New York -- after coming to California, then we went back to New York again. At this time when we go to New York we do the other circuit, the Loews circuit -- The Loews circuit then we'd go to the Poli circuit.
Who was booking you at that time?
Nazarro, through the other offices, you know. Maybe we
had two or three offices booking us, you know.
Were you accompanying their act at that time --
No, no, we were doing by ourselves, we're working by ourselves now.
